paper_metadata.title: Role of Quantitative EEG and EEG Reactivity in Traumatic Brain Injury

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study used a consecutive sampling method in a specialized ICU setting with clear inclusion/exclusion criteria. Baseline characteristics were well-defined, and the recruitment period and location were explicitly stated.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: consecutive patients with sTBI admitted from February 2017 to June 2018 to neurosurgery intensive care unit (N-ICU) and general ICU at Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.
items.reasoning: The authors specify the clinical setting (ICU), the condition (sTBI), and the specific hospital, providing a clear source population.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: A prospective study was conducted on consecutive patients with sTBI
items.reasoning: Consecutive recruitment is the gold standard for limiting selection bias in prognosis studies.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: admitted from February 2017 to June 2018
items.reasoning: The start and end dates are clearly provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: neurosurgery intensive care unit (N-ICU) and general ICU at Xiangya Hospital of Central South University.
items.reasoning: The specific units and the institution are named.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: The inclusion criteria were as follows: All patients older than 18 years having a Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score of less than or equal to 8, and the onset of brain injury within 14 days... The exclusion criteria were as follows: (1) a known history of neurological disorders; (2) EEG recorded during sedation... (3) burst-suppression; and (4) patients lost to follow-up.
items.reasoning: Criteria are specific, including age, GCS threshold, time from onset, and clinical exclusions like sedation levels.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 67 patients with sTBI were enrolled in this study. Eleven patients had to be excluded... 56 patients were included in this study
items.reasoning: The flow of participants is described; 56/67 (83.5%) were included in the final analysis, which is above the 80% threshold.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Table 1. The Characteristics of the 56 Patients. Age, years, mean ± SD 54.8 ± 11.9; Gender, male/female, n 36/20; Time from onset to EEG recording...
items.reasoning: Key demographics and clinical status (GCS, aEEG grade) are provided in Table 1.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study reports a low attrition rate (3 patients lost to follow-up out of 67). Reasons for exclusion are clearly documented, and the follow-up period is consistent for all participants.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: 56 patients were included in this study... 3 patients were lost to follow-up
items.reasoning: Only 3/67 (4.5%) were lost to follow-up, which is very low.

items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The text mentions they were lost to follow-up but does not describe specific attempts (e.g., phone calls, record searches) to reach them.

items.label: Reasons and potential impact of subjects lost to follow-up
items.prompt: Reasons for loss to follow-up are provided.
items.evidence_snippet: 2 patients died of severe infection, 3 patients were lost to follow-up, 2 patients appeared burst suppression, and 4 patients presented epileptic status.
items.reasoning: The study explicitly lists reasons for exclusion/attrition.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The prognostic factors (qEEG and EEG-R) are defined with high technical specificity. Measurement was standardized across the cohort, and the RAV scoring was performed by a blinded assessor, which significantly reduces measurement bias.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The RAV is calculated using the formula: (peak RA − trough RA)/(peak RA + trough RA)... EEG-R was classified as reactive (present) or nonreactive (absent)
items.reasoning: Mathematical formulas and clinical definitions for all qEEG parameters and EEG-R are provided.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: scored for their variability (RAV) by a physician blinded to the clinical condition and patient outcomes... EEG-R was assessed by 2 certified neurologists
items.reasoning: Blinding for RAV and dual-assessor consensus for EEG-R are strong methodological safeguards.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: RAV was divided into 4 grades in the study... An average baseline of the RA trend was set at a median value of RA during 8 to 12 hours.
items.reasoning: The study uses established grading systems (Synek, RAV grades) rather than creating post-hoc cut-points.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: Bedside qEEG (Nicolet Monitor, Natus Inc) was performed within 14 days of onset... The electrodes were placed according to the international 10-20 system
items.reasoning: Standardized equipment and electrode placement were used for all patients.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: 56 patients were included in this study
items.reasoning: The analysis includes the full final sample for the primary prognostic factors.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: The paper does not explicitly mention how missing data within the 8-12 hour monitoring period was handled, though it mentions excluding artifacts.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (GOS) is a validated, standard tool in TBI research. The timing of assessment (3 months) is clear, and the binary categorization of 'good' vs 'poor' prognosis is standard.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: The Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) score... was used. The scores 3, 4, and 5 of GOS were defined as awakened and good prognosis, and score 1 and 2 as unawakened and poor prognosis.
items.reasoning: The GOS is clearly defined and the follow-up duration (3 months) is specified.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: The outcomes of all patients were assessed for 3 months after entry into the study.
items.reasoning: While GOS is a valid tool, the paper does not explicitly state if the outcome assessors were blinded to the qEEG/EEG-R results, which is a potential source of bias.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: The outcomes of all patients were assessed for 3 months after entry into the study.
items.reasoning: The same scale and timeframe were applied to the entire cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study used multivariable logistic regression to adjust for some factors, the sample size (n=56) is small for the number of variables initially considered. Additionally, while sedation was an exclusion criterion for high doses, the authors admit it remains a potential confounder.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured

items.evidence_snippet: age, gender, GCS score, pupillary light reflex on admission to the ICU, aEEG, RBP, RAV, SE, and EEG-R.
items.reasoning: Key clinical confounders were measured, but specific treatment interventions (e.g., surgery types, ICP management) were not detailed as covariates.

items.label: Appropriate Accounting for Confounding
items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the study design (e.g., matching for key variables, stratification, or initial assembly of comparable groups).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG recorded during sedation maintained by greater than 2 mg/h of midazolam or the infusion dose of propofol higher than 1.2 mg/kg/h [excluded]
items.reasoning: The study used exclusion criteria to limit the confounding effect of heavy sedation, but did not use matching or stratification.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).
items.evidence_snippet: variables that were significantly different between the 2 groups in univariate analysis (GCS, aEEG, RBP, RAV, SE, and EEG-R) were entered into multivariate regression analysis.
items.reasoning: Multivariable adjustment was performed, although the small sample size limits the robustness of the model.
